data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, the name Naylaa carries deep spiritual significance as it is derived from the Arabic word 'nahlah', meaning 'star' or 'night'. The Quran mentions the name in the story of Maryam (Mary), who gave birth to 'Isa (Jesus) under a palm tree by the riverbank. Allah said to her, "Whatever food you get, eat it, and whatever water you drink, drink it, but let there touch no man of man or jinn, except either of those whom you have opened the way. Then if they forsake you, there will come to you Isha' (a man from the people of the town) following in the traces of those believers. He will renew your faith with the Faith of your people, be steadfast, and do not grieve, for every grief will be touched with mercy.' (Quran 19:24-28). The reference to "Isha' - the man from the town" in this passage is believed to have inspired the name Naylaa, as 'Isha' literally means 'night', and thus, the name Naylaa can be understood as a symbol of guidance and protection from the darkness and uncertainty of unknown people or situations, just as the stars in the night sky provide guidance and navigation. Additionally, the night is a time of spiritual reflection and contemplation in Islamic tradition, so the name Naylaa can also be seen as a reminder of the blessings and guidance that come from Allah during the night.
